history.dynasty: Vijayanagara (Yelahanka Nada Prabhus); legend attributes origin to sages Gautama Maharishi and Bharadwaja Muni
history.period: 16th century CE (renovation/expansion by Kempe Gowda I); Vedic-period origin per local legend (UNVERIFIED)
history.summary: Rock-cut cave temple ('gavi' = cave in Kannada) dedicated to Lord Shiva, carved into a monolithic granite boulder at Gavipuram in Bengaluru. Legend holds that Gautama Maharishi and Bharadwaja Muni worshipped here in the Vedic period; the present structure was built by Kempe Gowda I, founder of Bengaluru, in the 16th century after he was released from five years' imprisonment by Rama Raya. Its forecourt has monolithic pillars supporting stone discs of the Sun and Moon and pillars topped with seated Nandi; on Makara Sankranti (and for a few days around 26 November-2 December) the setting sun's rays pass through the horns of Nandi and illuminate the sanctum lingam for about an hour - a feat of archaeo-astronomy documented in Current Science. Paintings by Thomas and William Daniell (1792) record 18th-century renovations. The shrine is a protected monument under the Karnataka Ancient and Historical Monuments Act 1961.

name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
town_description: Bengaluru, capital of Karnataka, is India's technology hub ('Silicon Valley of India') with a much older history as a market town founded by Kempe Gowda in 1537. Gavipuram (Kempegowda Nagar) in the city's south is one of its oldest quarters, anchored by this 16th-century cave temple and the nearby Bugle Rock park, standing in contrast to the modern metropolis around it.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, approx. 40 km north (verify); taxis and airport buses (Vayu Vajra) to the city.
travel.railway: Bengaluru City Junction (Krantivira Sangolli Rayanna), approx. 8 km (verify); nearest suburban stations include Bengaluru South (verify).
travel.road: In Gavipuram, Kempegowda Nagar, south Bengaluru; well connected by BMTC buses and autos from Bangalore Bus Station and central Bengaluru.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Makara Sankranti (13-16 January) for the famous solar-illumination phenomenon - expect very heavy crowds in the late afternoon.
